Rimsky-Korsakov: Practical Manual of Harmony

The modulation examples, with Roman numerals under the notes

The 37 modulation examples from Rimsky-Korsakov’s Practical Manual of Harmony, short four-voice progressions from C major or A minor to another key, with the Roman-numeral analysis under the notes (When in Rome). Play each one.

Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov’s harmony textbook was first published in St Petersburg in 1886. It teaches modulation through short four-voice progressions, and these are its modulation examples: each starts in C major or A minor and reaches a new key, a few go there and back. They are grouped by the book’s example number; the letters are its variants.

How to read the labels and use the scores: Analysed Scores. For modulation itself, see Chapter 22.

5a. C major to F major

5b. C major to F minor

5c. A minor to C major

5d. A minor to C major

5e. A minor to D minor

5f. A minor to E minor

5g. A minor to E major

5h. A minor to F major

NoteFor teachers
  • Source: the notes and analyses are the DDMAL Key Modulation Dataset’s encodings of the book’s examples (Néstor Nápoles López and others), translated automatically to RomanText and copied into When in Rome. scripts/when-in-rome/build.mjs reads the MusicXML (src/rimsky), and every note was checked against music21’s reading of the same files.
  • Example numbers are the dataset’s (3-5a and so on; the 3 is dropped here). They have not been checked against a printed edition.
  • Not edited: the analyses are an automated translation and are shown as they are.

For students

Gotham, Mark, et al. When in Rome: A Meta-Corpus of Functional Harmony. GitHub. github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome. The analyses on this page (RomanText files), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

Hutchinson, Robert. “Modulation.” Music Theory for the 21st-Century Classroom, ch. 22, U of Puget Sound. musictheory.pugetsound.edu/mt21c/Modulation.html. Tonicization against modulation, closely related keys, diatonic and chromatic pivot chords, and direct, common-tone and sequential modulation.

Rimsky-Korsakov, Nikolay. Practical Manual of Harmony. A. Büttner, 1886. IMSLP. imslp.org/wiki/Practical_Manual_of_Harmony_(Rimsky-Korsakov,_Nikolay). The book whose modulation examples are on the Rimsky-Korsakov page; IMSLP has scans of later editions.

For teachers

Nápoles López, Néstor, et al. Key Modulation Dataset. GitHub (DDMAL). github.com/DDMAL/key_modulation_dataset. The encodings and analyses of the textbook examples, translated to RomanText by Nápoles López and copied into When in Rome.
